name: Blind Hunter
summary: The Blind Hunter is an elusive, albino bat that roosts deep within Razorfen Kraul. Unlike the ordinary bats nesting near the cavern entrances, this rare creature prowls the sunless depths of the quilboar redoubt.

sections.title: Depths of the Kraul
sections.body: Razorfen Kraul is riddled with winding briars and dark subterranean caverns. While common Kraul bats roost nearer to the surface where faint light filters in from the outside world, the Blind Hunter has adapted entirely to the furthest, darkest alcoves of the tangle. Its pale, albino hide and milky gaze are likely the result of generations spent completely isolated from natural sunlight.

sections.title: A Rare Quarry
sections.body: True to its name, scholars and scouts believe the creature has lost most or all of its conventional eyesight, relying instead on keen senses of hearing and echolocation to track prey through the gloom. It rarely shows itself, appearing only on occasion to hunt through the dense thickets, making an encounter with this phantom beast a prized occurrence among cavern explorers.

faq.answer: The Blind Hunter is a rare albino bat dwelling in the deepest, pitch-black tunnels of Razorfen Kraul. It is remarkably pale and elusive compared to the common cavern bats found closer to the entrance.

faq.q: Where does the Blind Hunter appear?
faq.answer: It dwells in the shadowy interior paths of Razorfen Kraul, nesting well past the threshold where outside daylight fades away entirely.

faq.q: Is the Blind Hunter actually blind?
faq.answer: While naturalists and adventurers suspect it is truly blind due to its milky eyes and deep-cave habitat, its hunting ability remains razor-sharp, relying on keen hearing and echolocation in the darkness.

faq.q: Can hunters tame the Blind Hunter?
faq.answer: Yes, beastmasters capable of managing winged predators can tame the Blind Hunter, making it a distinctive pale companion for those patient enough to track it down.

faq.q: Why is the Blind Hunter white?
faq.answer: It is an albino specimen whose coloration likely developed from living in perpetual darkness far from the reach of the sun, unlike bats that venture near the cave mouth.

faq.q: How does it differ from regular Kraul bats?
faq.answer: Ordinary Kraul bats possess typical dark coloration and live nearer to the entrance where light still penetrates, whereas the Blind Hunter is pale, reclusive, and adapted strictly to deep subterranean tunnels.

angles.text: For beastmasters traversing the Barrens, the Blind Hunter represents a prize quarry—either as a rare albino beast to tame or as a source of well-crafted subterranean bows.
